item.title: Direct Restoration of Spent LiFePO4 via Lattice Defect Correction and Nitrogen-Doped Interface Engineering
item.description:
بازسازی مستقیم LiFePO4 مستعمل با اتانول‌آمین و LiNO3، نقص‌های شبکه و جای‌خالی لیتیوم را اصلاح کرده و لایه سطحی N-doped ایجاد می‌کند و ظرفیت 106.04 mAh g–1 با حفظ ۱۰۰٪ در ۵۰۰ چرخه حاصل می‌شود.
Nano Letters | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using ethanolamine with LiNO3 for synergistic direct regeneration: ethanolamine gently removes surface impurities, reduces Fe(III) to Fe(II), fills Li vacancies via low steric hindrance, and acts as an in situ nitrogen source for N-doped interfacial engineering. This enables restored LiFePO4 with excellent rate performance (106.04 mAh g–1 at 5.0 C) and 100% retention over 500 cycles, plus economic and environmental benefits.
🏷 LiFePO4 regeneration · spent cathode · lattice defect · nitrogen doping · direct recycling

item.title: Direct Experimental Quantification of Intrinsic Capacitive Properties of Monolayer Ti3C2T x MXene
item.description:
خازن ذاتی تک‌لایه Ti3C2Tx MXene به‌صورت تجربی اندازه‌گیری شد و سهم شبه‌خازن در الکترولیت اسیدی حدود ۴۵٪ و در الکترولیت‌های یون فلز قلیایی کمتر از ۱۰٪ تعیین شد.
Nano Letters | 🔬 Research Article
💡 First direct experimental quantification of intrinsic capacitance of monolayer Ti3C2Tx MXene via optimized flake protection and parasitic-capacitance shielding. Reports 141 μF cm–2 in acid, 61–74 μF cm–2 in alkali electrolytes; pseudocapacitance ~45% in acid but <10% in alkali; lower proton-transfer activation energy enables pseudocapacitive storage. Establishes a benchmark for monolayer MXene interfaces.
🏷 Ti3C2Tx MXene · monolayer capacitance · pseudocapacitance · electric double layer · proton transfer

ACS Energy Letters | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a coordination-driven strategy using π–d conjugated small molecules (BTD-M) with p-type triphenylamine ligands, thermodynamically locking discrete molecules against dissolution while preserving active-site access. Significance: BTD-Cu enables a narrow 0.7 eV bandgap, near-theoretical capacity (134 mAh g–1), and a symmetric all-organic dual-ion battery with 2.4 V average voltage and >1000-cycle life, establishing a platform for insoluble organic battery design.

item.title: Ionic Microenvironment Regulator Enables Enhanced Anion Trapping in Cationic Poly(Ionic Liquid) Solid Electrolyte for Low‐Temperature Lithium Metal Batteries
item.description:

Advanced Functional Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using methyl trifluoromethanesulfonate (TMS) as an ionic microenvironment regulator in a cationic poly(ionic liquid) solid electrolyte, which enhances lithium salt dissociation and induces anion trapping via modulated charge distribution. This enables uniform Li deposition and fast Li+ transport at −15°C, yielding high-voltage batteries with 89.8% retention over 500 cycles and 80.1% over 800 cycles—advancing low-temperature solid-state lithium metal battery design.

item.title: Bioinspired Repurposing of Lisinopril: A Clinical ACE Inhibitor as a Trace Dual‐Functional Additive for Ultrastable Aqueous Zinc‐Ion Batteries
item.description:
داروی لیزینوپریل به‌عنوان افزودنی کم‌مقدار الکترولیت، با تنظیم پوسته حل‌پوشی و تشکیل SEI پایدار، پایداری و بازدهی بالای باتری آبی Zn-ion را ممکن ساخت.
Advanced Functional Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Repurposing lisinopril, a clinical ACE inhibitor, as a trace dual-functional electrolyte additive for aqueous zinc-ion batteries is novel. Its multidentate amphiphilic structure forms a gradient hybrid interphase, regulates Zn2+ solvation, and buffers pH, enabling ultrastable cycling (99.78% efficiency, 2400 h, 10,000-cycle full cells). This demonstrates converting pharmaceutical Zn-binding motifs into function-oriented additives for durable batteries.
🏷 aqueous zinc-ion battery · lisinopril additive · solid electrolyte interphase · Zn dendrite · solvation regulation
